beats.say: [curious] This patch of desert is one of the only places on Earth that no country wants.
beats.label: NO COUNTRY WANTS IT

beats.say: [excited] It's called Bir Tawil, squeezed right between Egypt and Sudan.
beats.label: BIR TAWIL

beats.say: Back in 1899, the British drew a perfectly straight border right here.
beats.label: 1899 BORDER

beats.say: [sighs] But three years later, they drew a second one. And this one bends.
beats.label: 1902 BORDER

beats.say: That left two pieces of land: tiny Bir Tawil, and the Halaib Triangle, ten times bigger, right on the Red Sea.
Here's the trap. [whispers] Whoever claims Bir Tawil has to give up Halaib.
[laughs] So Egypt and Sudan both say: Bir Tawil? Not ours!
No towns. No water. No people. And no country.
In 2014, an American dad even planted a flag here, so his daughter could be a real princess.

card.query: flag on a pole in the desert
card.subject: flag

beats.say: So today, it's still nobody's land. [whispers] Totally up for grabs.
beats.label: UP FOR GRABS
